description: Fixed 12-host Kepler Quarter 6 convenience cohort to compare the identical, unchanged localized-step heuristic on original SAP_FLUX vs NASA-corrected PDCSAP_FLUX. Source labels are archival SPSD quality bit 1024, not confirmed exhaustive ground truth.
primary_question: At independently archived SAP_QUALITY bit-1024 events in an untouched star cohort, do detection warnings differ between original and NASA-corrected flux when the same fixed detector and timestamps are used?
selection: Public NASA-listed Kepler hosts selected for Q6 before reading these target light curves. Target IDs are held fixed; files missing from the official quarter archive remain planned failures and are never substituted. No events/epochs or steps were examined to choose the cohort. The known positive KIC 7461601 is excluded.
design_status: One exploratory independent observational cohort; targets are a purposive sample of known Kepler sources, not a random survey sample, and may contain real planets/stellar variability.

targets.identification: KIC 7960363; Kepler data handbook earlier Q1 example, here tests a different preselected Q6 file

explicit_exclusions: Existing previous-study calibration, frozen 13-target binary/planet cohort, six Q8 localized-step held-out stars, and KIC 7461601 published Q6 case. No overlap planned.
data_source: NASA MAST official Kepler Quarter 6 long-cadence DR25 FITS, using exactly corresponding SAP_FLUX, PDCSAP_FLUX, TIME, SAP_QUALITY rows.
source_fetch: Existing bounded public MAST download implemented in real_kepler_lightcurve.fetch_kepler_quarter. Preserve original FITS SHA256.

processing.pair_policy: Retain exactly identical aligned rows where finite positive TIME, SAP_FLUX, and PDCSAP_FLUX; keep nonzero quality flags so the event is physically observable. This is distinct from planet-detection experiments that require quality==0.
processing.detrend: Same kepler_preprocessing.normalize_flux with unchanged 301-point median window, independently for SAP and PDCSAP.
processing.algorithm: Exact localized_discontinuity.localized_downward_step_mask and its settings loaded unchanged from LOCALIZED_STEP_STUDY_FROZEN_2026_11_07.json; no retraining, retuning or event-specific processing.

analysis.unit_of_evidence: Independent flagged event clusters nested within preselected host; do not count every flagged cadence as an independent event.
analysis.matching_rule: For each product separately, match predicted onsets to archival flagged event clusters without replacement, sorted by nearest absolute time offset, requiring abs difference <=0.22 days.
analysis.primary_metrics: Number of planned/available stars; SPSD bit-flagged event clusters; matched flagged event clusters for SAP and PDCSAP, both/baseline-only/PDC-only/neither, per-star counts. Report missing or absent SPSD event labels separately.
analysis.secondary_metrics: Unmatched step warnings per product (not false-positive rate); warnings per usable star; mask percentage; source hashes; median per-event matched time difference.
analysis.plot_policy: Create a per-star paired comparison and an event-centered source figure for the lowest KIC with a flagged event, if any, selected by KIC order before inspecting detection outcomes.
interpretation_limits: Kepler PDC is mission-grade and often corrects SPSDs; SAP and PDCSAP differences do not establish our detector beats it.
Mission quality bit 1024 is a fallible/incomplete event marker; unmatched warnings are not confirmed false alarms and bit-1024 flags do not equal planet labels.
Selected sources are known Kepler hosts, not representative random stars; a small number of quality flags may prevent useful sensitivity estimates.
The pipeline may use quality metadata, so archival flags are not statistically independent of correction activity.
One event cluster can produce multiple quality bits/cadences; cluster flagged epochs and use event-level matched pairs.
Retaining flagged rows is required to observe the defect but is not the science-quality policy used for planet injection studies.
Do not change thresholds or select new stars after seeing outcomes and then call the result an independent validation.
